gloss: to come and go; to pass each other

definitions.gloss: to come and go; to pass back and forth
definitions.explanation: To move back and forth in different directions, describing multiple people, vehicles, or things passing by one another. Evokes a scene of lively movement and traffic.

examples.japanese: {通|とお}りを{人|ひと}が{行|い}き{交|か}う。
examples.english: People come and go along the street.

examples.japanese: {港|みなと}には{大小|だいしょう}さまざまな{船|ふね}が{行|い}き{交|か}っていた。
examples.english: Ships of all sizes were coming and going in the harbor.

examples.japanese: {年末|ねんまつ}の{商店街|しょうてんがい}は、{買|か}い{物客|ものきゃく}が{忙|せわ}しなく{行|い}き{交|か}っていた。
examples.english: The shopping district at year's end was bustling with shoppers hurrying back and forth.

notes:
{行|い}き{交|か}う is an intransitive godan verb. A compound of {行|い}く (to go) and {交|か}う (to cross, to intersect).

ASPECT (ている):
{行|い}き{交|か}っている describes an ongoing scene of people or things moving back and forth.

PARTICLE PATTERNS:
- [person/vehicle]が{行|い}き{交|か}う (people/vehicles pass back and forth)
- [place]を{行|い}き{交|か}う (come and go through a place)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {人|ひと}が{行|い}き{交|か}う (people come and go)
- {車|くるま}が{行|い}き{交|か}う (cars pass back and forth)
- {情報|じょうほう}が{行|い}き{交|か}う (information is exchanged back and forth)

Often used to paint a vivid picture of a busy scene. Can also describe the exchange of messages, emails, or information flying back and forth between parties.
